body.statement: For every \(c\in\mathcal C_K\), the primal program defining \(V_c\) is feasible for every \(\xi\in\mathbb R^{S_c}\), and \[V_c(\xi)=\max\{\ell^\top\xi:|\ell^\top b_t|\le\theta_t^2\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal T_c\}.\] The dual feasible set is compact on \(\mathbf 1^\perp\), \(V_c\) is finite, convex, even, continuous, and positively homogeneous, and \(0<\kappa(c)\le1\). For rational \(c\), primal and dual optimizers and \(\kappa(c)\) are exactly rational and terminate under finite linear programming.
body.justification: The gauge is the finite-alphabet object that converts multi-arm response geometry into a scalar Airy coefficient.
body.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 3.1, has no response-alphabet linear program because its reduced experiment is scalar.
body.consumer: The exact primal-dual record supplies both the shrinkage score and the rational input to the finite certificate.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(d=|S_c|\), and regard the vectors \(b_t\) as columns of a \(d\)-by-\(2^d\) matrix \(A\).  For every active coordinate \(a\),
\[
e_a=b_{e_a}+b_{\mathbf 1},\qquad -e_a=b_{\mathbf 1-e_a}+b_{\mathbf 0}.
\]
Consequently, writing \(\xi_a=\xi_a^+-\xi_a^-\), where \(\xi_a^+=\max(\xi_a,0)\) and \(\xi_a^-=\max(-\xi_a,0)\), gives a nonnegative representation of \(\xi\).  This proves feasibility, and its cost is finite because \(\mathcal T_c\) is finite.

Let \(w_t=\theta_t^2\).  The primal problem is \(\min\{w^\top\lambda:A\lambda=\xi,\lambda\ge0\}\).  Its weak dual is
\[
\sup\{\ell^\top\xi:A^\top\ell\le w\}.
\]
For completeness, strong duality here follows directly from finite-dimensional separation.  The set
\[
\mathcal P=\{(A\lambda,w^\top\lambda+s):\lambda\ge0, s\ge0\}
\]
is a closed polyhedral cone.  If \(p\) is the primal value, separate \((\xi,p-\varepsilon)\) strictly from \(\mathcal P\).  The cone contains the vertical ray above \((\xi,p)\); hence the last separating coordinate is nonpositive, and it cannot be zero because both separated points have first coordinate \(\xi\).  Normalizing that coordinate to \(-1\), and then letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), produces dual-feasible \(\ell_\varepsilon\) with \(\ell_\varepsilon^\top\xi\ge p-\varepsilon\).  Weak duality supplies the reverse inequality, so the two values agree.  Because the complement map \(t\mapsto\mathbf 1-t\) sends \(b_t\) to \(-b_t\) and preserves \(\theta_t^2\), the pair of dual inequalities indexed by complementary types is exactly
\[
|\ell^\top b_t|\le\theta_t^2\quad(t\in\mathcal T_c).
\]

The types \(\mathbf 0\) and \(\mathbf 1\) have zero cost because \(\sum_a c_a=0\).  Their constraints imply \(\ell^\top\mathbf 1=0\).  The singleton type then gives
\[
|\ell_a|=|\ell^\top(e_a-\mathbf 1/2)|\le c_a^2.
\]
Thus the dual feasible set is a closed subset of the bounded box \(\prod_{a\in S_c}[-c_a^2,c_a^2]\), contained in \(\mathbf 1^\perp\); it is compact.  The displayed dual representation now shows that \(V_c\) is the support function of a nonempty compact centrally symmetric convex set.  Hence it is finite, convex, even, continuous, and positively homogeneous.

It remains to bound \(\kappa(c)\).  Let
\[
m_c=\min\{|\theta_t|:t\in\mathcal T_c,\ \theta_t\ne0\}.
\]
This minimum is positive because the alphabet is finite and the sign-pattern type below has nonzero score.  Every feasible representation of \(v\) obeys
\[
1=c^\top v=\sum_t\lambda_t\theta_t,
\]
and therefore
\[
\sum_t\lambda_t\theta_t^2
\ge m_c\sum_t\lambda_t|\theta_t|
\ge m_c\left|\sum_t\lambda_t\theta_t\right|=m_c.
\]
On the other hand, let \(t^+_a=1\) when \(c_a>0\) and \(t^+_a=0\) when \(c_a<0\).  The zero-sum and \(\ell^1\)-normalization assumptions give \(\sum_{c_a>0}c_a=1\), so
\[
b_{t^+}=s_c/2=v,\qquad \theta_{t^+}=1.
\]
The one-atom representation \(\lambda_{t^+}=1\) has cost one.  Thus \(0<m_c\le\kappa(c)\le1\).

Finally suppose that \(c\) is rational.  The matrix \(A\), the right side \(v\), and the costs \(w_t\) are rational.  An optimum occurs at a basic feasible solution: this follows by repeatedly removing a nonzero null direction from the positive support until its columns are linearly independent, choosing the sign that does not increase cost.  There are finitely many such supports, and exact Gaussian elimination enumerates their rational vertices.  The same finite enumeration applies to the compact rational dual polytope; successive rational linear programs select its lexicographically least optimizer.  Hence primal and dual optimizers and \(\kappa(c)\) are rational and are found after finitely many exact operations.
